claim: Wearables commonly diagnose conditions and support intervention
originalWording: Wearables commonly diagnose conditions and support intervention

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Computers embedded across watches, jewelry, and clothing routinely diagnose a broad range of acute and chronic medical conditions and guide intervention.
strict.rationale: Apple Watch Series 4 (2018) added FDA-cleared ECG/AFib classification and fall detection, and ~21% of US adults wore a smartwatch or tracker by 2019. However, Apple's own release emphasizes that AFib alerts are limited-purpose and cannot detect heart attacks, strokes, or most diseases, and diagnostic clothing and jewelry remain uncommon.
changedConditions: Enforces broad acute/chronic diagnostic coverage and the clothing/jewelry form factors in the 2019 passage

evidence.title: ECG app and irregular rhythm notification available on Apple Watch
evidence.note: AFib-related features are limited-purpose. The release expressly lists conditions they cannot detect; not general diagnosis or autonomous treatment.

evidence.title: Apple: Watch Series 4 health, ECG and fall detection
evidence.note: ECG/AFib classification, hard-fall detection and emergency calling; ECG deployment corroborated by December 2018 release O22. Not diagnosis of all diseases or autonomous treatment.

evidence.title: Pew: About one-in-five Americans use a smartwatch or fitness tracker
evidence.note: June 2019 US survey: 21% regularly wear one. Common does not mean majority, and US adult prevalence is not global prevalence.

reference.criterion: Common wearable monitors identify selected acute and chronic problems and trigger useful advice or intervention pathways.
reference.rationale: By late 2018 Apple Watch combined ECG/AFib classification, hard-fall detection and emergency calling; the 2019 wearable survey supports common adoption. Those capabilities satisfy a reasonable targeted-condition reading. The forecast did not demand diagnosis of every disease or removal of physicians.
